text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate on streaming-decode cluster (gpu-pool-3). 45% request drops in last 2m, affected region: us-west-2. Paging oncall: @alex. Paging SRE: @maya.

alex: On it. opening thread. any quick context?

maya: Seeing rapid memory growth on decode-worker pods during streaming responses. CUDA OOM logs spiking.

jordan: I'm seeing a lot of long-running streams where clients send max_tokens >> expected. Looks like some clients hit a bad prompt loop — unbounded emission.

liz: Support reports a customer reported 502s and half their sessions dropped ~5 mins ago. Ticket #INC-8812 linked: https://redwood.ops/t/INC-8812

alex: Triage plan: 1) throttle new streaming sessions to reduce load 2) apply emergency config to override max_tokens to 1024 for streaming route 3) fallback routing to cpu-quant model variant for bursty sessions.

maya: Throttling via rate-limit policy now: /v1/streaming -> soft limit 20 rps for affected pool. Confirming hydra rule applied.

jordan: Pushing patch to router to honor per-request max_tokens cap override. Command:

```
# emergency override
curl -X POST https://control-plane/configs/overrides -d '{"route":"/v1/streaming","max_tokens_cap":1024}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

alex: Applied override, ack. Starting gradual rollback of long-lived streams? or drain nodes?

maya: Recommend draining the worst nodes, but drain causes reconnect storms. Instead: evict top memory consumers using live probe then restart process. Running: `kubectl exec -n inference -c agent decode-worker-37 -- pkill -f decode_loop` to restart decode loop on offending pods.

ken: Infra telemetry shows 6 pods with >95% GPU memory and growing. I'll cordon those nodes and restart pods sequentially to avoid capacity hole.

jordan: Also enabling model fallback: any stream exceeding 30s or 500 tokens will be routed to smaller-quantized variant (gptx-small-8q) to reduce footprint.

customer-ops: Can we estimate customer impact window? Support needs to update customers.

liz: Based on ticket counts, ~12 customers affected with intermittent drops. Highest severity: one enterprise saw 40% of sessions drop. ETA for mitigation: 8-12 minutes.

alex: Executing fallback switch now. Will monitor error rate and p99 latency.

incident-bot: CONFIG UPDATE: route /v1/streaming fallback -> gptx-small-8q (immediate).

maya: After fallback and throttles p50 latency stable, p99 spiky but error rate dropping from 45% -> 8% in last 3 minutes. GPU OOM logs still appear on a couple pods, but decreasing.

jordan: I see one recurring pattern in logs: client sends function_call loop, stop condition missing, server keeps generating. Example log snippet:

```
stream-id=abc123 msg="emit 2048 tokens" user_prompt_len=128 max_tokens=0
decode: kv_cache_growth=+1.2GB tokens_generated=2100
CUDA Error: out of memory at decode_step 2046
```

maya: That max_tokens=0 misinterpretation seems key. Router wasn't enforcing default cap when client passed 0. We'll add defensive validation in next minor release.

alex: For immediate safety, I pushed a validation patch to edge that treats max_tokens<=0 as 256. Patch id: PATCH-9321. Hot-redeploying to edge nodes now.

ken: Node restarts in progress. Rolling restart of 6 pods, 30s between restarts. Observability: GPU memory usage trending down.

incident-bot: ONCALL-HANDOFF: @alex available for 30m, @maya standing by for SRE followup, page will update on status changes.

customer-ops: Support update going out: "We've applied mitigations to reduce streaming errors (throttles, model fallback). We expect intermittent reconnects while nodes restart. Engineers are monitoring."

liz: Sent update to impacted customers at 14:38 PT.

jordan: Confirmed that after fallback and validation, no new OOMs logged in last 6 minutes. Remaining errors appear to be reconnects timed out.

maya: Marking incident scope: cause = client-triggered unbounded generation + router not enforcing max_tokens default -> memory surge -> GPU OOM -> request drops. Mitigations = throttling, max_tokens override, model fallback, restart pods.

alex: Raising postmortem ticket and action items. Quick list: 1) enforce max_tokens bounds in edge/router 2) add server-side guard to cap continuous streams 3) add metric for per-stream token emission rate 4) update docs for integrations about max_tokens=0 behavior 5) test chaos scenarios for streaming.

sam: Product note: need to ensure SDKs set sane defaults; will add warnings in changelog.

customer-ops: Any residual customer-level data loss?

liz: No persisted data lost. Sessions dropped; customers saw partial responses. We'll offer logs and regenerate tokens for impacted requests if requested.

alex: Moving to recovery phase. Will keep thread open for postmortem drafting. If error rate holds <1% for 15m, we'll close page.

incident-bot: METRIC: error_rate(/v1/streaming) = 0.9% (window 5m). Alerts will auto-resolve if sustained.

maya: I'll collect logs and create initial timeline for postmortem. Assigning action owners.

alex: Thanks team. Good job triaging. :thumbsup:

customer-ops: Customer update queued for 15:05 PT with root cause summary and remediation steps.

jordan: Follow-up: I'll add a CI test that simulates client generating 5k tokens and ensure streaming circuit-breaker trips.

ken: Infra follow-up: add GPU memory pressure alert with severity > p95 so we can preempt.

maya: Closing notes: incident classified P2, no data breach, customer impact limited to partial session drops. Postmortem timeline assigned.

alex: Closing thread in 20m unless new regressions.

incident-bot: "
